title: t5 (glassbox-bench seed-3): three-way comparison of count(ta) vs count(mo)
behavior: Input BOS + 6 tokens from {ta, mo, la, me, ba, le}; at the last position the model outputs one of K / S / U.
summary: The model outputs U if 'ta' occurs more often than 'mo' in the 6 input tokens, S if it occurs less often, and K if the counts are equal; the other four symbols are ignored. The rule agrees with the model on 200/200 held-out inputs (V0001, local-full, full precision). The circuit is head 1.0 (collects ta), head 1.2 (collects mo), and all three MLP layers; the other ten heads are inert. Circuit ablated: metric -0.0004, accuracy 0.35 (chance for 3 classes); everything else ablated: metric 1.0, accuracy 1.0. All numbers are from the local-full backend.
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    seq = tokens[1:]                 # drop BOS
    n_ta = seq.count(7)              # head 1.0: attends BOS + every 'ta' (E0008, E0011)
    n_mo = seq.count(6)              # head 1.2: attends BOS + every 'mo' (E0007, E0012)
    # mlp0 (before the heads) and mlp1, mlp2 (after) are all required (E0014)
    if n_ta > n_mo: return 10        # 'U'
    if n_ta < n_mo: return 9         # 'S'
    return 8                         # 'K'

claims.text: The model performs a deterministic 3-class behaviour (clean accuracy 1.0 on 200 prompts).
The function is: U if count(ta) > count(mo), S if count(ta) < count(mo), K if equal. This rule matches the model on 200/200 held-out inputs (null agreement 0.33).
Head 1.0 is the sole carrier of the ta count: in a ta-only contrast, patching head 1.0 alone restores the clean output completely (effect 1.0; every other head 0.0).
Head 1.2 is the sole carrier of the mo count: in a mo-only contrast, patching head 1.2 alone restores the clean output completely (effect 1.0; every other head 0.0).

Each of the two heads splits attention between BOS and its matching tokens: with one ta (resp. mo) at position 3, attention from the last position is 0.5 on BOS and 0.5 on that token, 0 elsewhere. The BOS share thus encodes 1/(1+count).
Heads 1.0 and 1.2 are necessary: joint mean ablation takes the metric to -0.02 of clean.
The other ten heads (0.0-0.3, 1.1, 1.3, 2.0-2.3) play no part: joint mean ablation of all ten leaves the metric at 1.0.
All three MLP layers are necessary: mean-ablating mlp0, mlp1 or mlp2 alone takes the metric to -0.02, 0.0 and 0.002.

The token's information stays at its own position through layer 0 and is at the last position before layer 2: resid_pre patching has effect 1.0 at (layer 0, pos 2), (layer 1, pos 2), (layer 2, pos 6) and 0 everywhere else. So the move to the last position happens in layer 1.

The circuit {1.0, 1.2, mlp0, mlp1, mlp2} is necessary and sufficient on held-out data: ablating it gives metric -0.0004 / accuracy 0.35; ablating the other 10 components gives metric 1.0 / accuracy 1.0; both beat their null distributions.

nodes.label: mlp0: per-token preprocessing (required; exact feature not resolved)
head 1.0: attend BOS + every ta -> ta count at last pos
head 1.2: attend BOS + every mo -> mo count at last pos

limitations: The individual computations of mlp0, mlp1 and mlp2 are not resolved: they are shown to be necessary (E0014), but which one converts attention shares to counts and which one compares is not measured.

One pre-registered prediction (E0013) was inconclusive: I assumed mlp_out patching was position-resolved; it patches all positions. Its by-product (each MLP's output alone restores the ta contrast) is suggestive of a serial chain mlp0 -> 1.0 -> mlp1 -> mlp2 but was not a pre-registered claim.
The edges mlp0 -> heads (key vs value) are inferred, not path-patched: path_patching with an MLP sender raised an error and was not run.
Contrast and attention experiments used small hand-written prompt sets (6-12 prompts); the dataset-level claims use 200 prompts.
The function was verified on 200 sampled inputs out of 46656 possible; not exhaustive.
open_questions: What exactly does mlp0 write at each token position, and does head 1.0/1.2 read it through keys or values?
How do mlp1 and mlp2 divide the work of turning two 1/(1+n) attention shares into a 3-way comparison?
